components.name: alert
components.description: Inline callout for operation results and system messages.
usage: Pick variant by severity: success | warning | danger | info | neutral (default).
Slots: AlertTitle (outcome), optional AlertHeadline (specific cause, e.g. the failed file), AlertDescription (next step).
AlertAction with a `Button variant="secondaryCta"` for follow-ups (View Logs).

components.name: aspect-ratio
components.description: Fixed-ratio container for media and placeholders.
usage: `<AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9}>` wrapping an image, video, or bg-muted placeholder.

components.name: avatar
components.description: User or entity avatar with an image and an initials fallback.
usage: Always compose Root + Fallback: `Avatar.Root` on its own renders an empty circle. The fallback is what shows while the image loads, when there is no `src`, and when the image 404s — so initials (`{user.name.split(' ').map((p) => p[0]).join('')}`) belong there even when you expect a photo.
Image: `Avatar.Image src={user.avatarUrl} alt={user.name}` — it is a real ``, so `alt` is yours to pass and a missing one is an accessibility violation. Use the person's name, not "avatar".

Size: `sm` (28px) for dense chrome like the side-nav profile row, `default` (36px) for lists and headers, `lg` (48px) for a profile or detail header. The size lands on `data-size` and the fallback's type scales off it through `group-data-[size=…]/avatar`, so overriding the root's `size-*` by hand desynchronises the two — add a size variant instead.

Shape: `circle` for people, `squircle` (12px radius at every size) for non-human entities (an org, a workspace, a model) so the two read apart at a glance. The radius is deliberately generous — at `sm` the squircle sits close to a circle, which is the intended look.

Skipping the loading flash: pass `loadingStatus="loaded"` when the image is already cached or inlined, which shows it immediately instead of flashing the fallback. It is bindable, so `bind:loadingStatus` also reads the outcome (`loading` | `loaded` | `error`) if the caller needs to react to a broken image.

Stacking (“who is on this session”): a `flex -space-x-2` row plus `*:data-[slot=avatar]:ring-2 *:data-[slot=avatar]:ring-background *:data-[slot=avatar]:border-0` on the container. The ring is what cuts each avatar out of the one behind it, and it hangs off `data-slot`, so separation stays a container concern rather than a prop. Drop the border in a stack: the root's `border-border` sits just inside the ring, so leaving it on renders a grey rim against a white gap against the next rim, and the overlap reads muddy. Stack images, not initials — the overlap covers each avatar's trailing edge, which a face survives and two letters do not.

components.name: badge
components.description: Small pill for a run's status, a selected item, or a step number — nothing else.
usage: Restraint: a badge is for state the user acts on, not decoration. Do not badge categories, tags, counts, model names, versions, units or metadata — write them as plain text (`text-muted-foreground` for secondary). One status badge per item at most, and never a badge next to text that already says the same thing.

Status: `variant="status"` colored by a status token on the text alone, e.g. class="text-atai-good" (Completed), atai-critical (Failed), atai-warning (Interrupted), atai-neutral (Running), muted-foreground (Pending). The outline follows the text colour, so never pass a `border-*` class or remove the outline.
Size: `size="sm"` gives the status pill smaller type and tighter spacing for tight spaces (cards, tables) or inline with text; defaults to `size="default"`.
Selection: `variant="selection"` for dismissible picks, with an embedded `Button variant="ghost" size="inline" visibility="dimmed"` X icon to remove.

Step: `variant="step"` is the filled circle that numbers the steps of an ordered procedure, e.g. `<Badge variant="step" aria-hidden="true">{i + 1}</Badge>` leading each row with `flex items-center gap-2`. Pass the number only, 1-based; one digit is a circle and more digits stretch it into a pill of the same height. Hide it from assistive tech when the row's label already names the step. `size="sm"` (16px) suits dense lists and `text-xs` labels; `size="lg"` (24px) steps set beside larger type.
Spacing: the badge carries no outer margin — the container owns the gap (e.g. `flex gap-2`). For the rare trailing-edge case, add `class="-mr-1"` at the call site.

components.name: breadcrumb
components.description: Hierarchical navigation trail for nested console flows (e.g. user management).
usage: Compose Breadcrumb.Root > Breadcrumb.List > Breadcrumb.Item; place a Breadcrumb.Separator between items (defaults to a chevron, override via children).
Ancestors are links (`Breadcrumb.Link href="..."`); the current location is the non-link `Breadcrumb.Page` (carries aria-current="page").
Collapse long trails by putting `Breadcrumb.Ellipsis` inside a Breadcrumb.Item. Typography is mono/uppercase to match the `backToDashboard` button.

components.name: button
components.description: Action trigger for every emphasis level; renders an <a> when href is set. `loading` prop swaps in a spinner.
usage: cta — filled primary action (Create, Submit, modal confirm); one per view. `size="sm"` in toolbars and dialog footers.
secondaryCta — capitalized text action, underline on hover (Learn More, alert/banner follow-ups).
outline — secondary action paired against a cta (Cancel/Close in dialog footers); also `width="full"` add-file buttons in pickers.
ghost + size="icon" — quiet icon action everywhere: row actions, pager arrows, sidebar collapse, card headers (copy, dismiss).
accent + size="icon" — quiet icon control that gains a bg on hover (steppers, profile/theme triggers).
destructive + size="icon" — delete/end action, turns red on hover; add visibility="hover" inside list rows so it only appears on row hover.
floating + size="overlay" — backdrop-blurred control floating over media or scrolling panels (sort selector).
link — inline text link; size="inline" flows inside prose (empty states). announcement — babyblue brand pill.
typography="mono" uppercases label text (dialog footer CTAs); width="full" for full-width form buttons.

components.name: card
components.description: Surface container with Header/Title/Action/Content/Footer sub-parts.
usage: Detail panel: `variant="info"` + Card.Header (Card.Title + Card.Action icon) + Card.Content layout="stack" holding Label sectionHeader → mono value pairs (Job Details, dialog notes).
Grid tile: `variant="status"` for clickable job/model status cards in dashboard grids (pass href); `variant="intro"` for hero/landing cards.

Card.Title capitalizes by default. Pass `titleCase={false}` when the title is user-authored and must render verbatim (agent names, filenames) — never reach in with `[&_[data-slot=card-title]]:normal-case`.
Single-metric status cards often need no CardHeader — omit when content is self-explanatory.

components.name: chart
components.description: Chart.Container + Chart.Tooltip wrappers around layerchart for custom charts (prefer sensor-chart / scatter-chart when they fit).
usage: Wrap every layerchart in `<Chart.Container config={...} class="aspect-auto h-[220px] w-full">`; config maps data keys to { label, color: 'var(--chart-N)' } (chart-1…chart-5).
layerchart is pinned to an exact prerelease — never loosen it.

components.name: checkbox
components.description: Binary selection control (bits-ui).
usage: `bind:checked` + aria-label; for selectable file rows wrap checkbox + name + size in a <label> row, selected state via bg-atai-brand-babyblue/60.

components.name: codeblock
components.description: Syntax-highlighted code display (CodeBlock, shiki; yaml/json/python/shell) and editable code field with JSON-schema validation for YAML (CodeBlockEditor).
usage: `<CodeBlock code language="yaml" />` for read-only code (border built in). `language` accepts `"yaml" | "json" | "python" | "shell"` — use `"shell"` for bash/sh/curl snippets. Theme switches are CSS-only — no {#key} wrapper needed. Grows to content by default and never clips: whenever its height is constrained — by a `max-h-*` class, by a flex/grid parent like `Dialog.Body`, or by the `maxHeight`/`scroll` props — the internal scroller shows a scrollbar instead. To cap it yourself pass `maxHeight="20rem"` (any CSS length) or the `scroll` shorthand (=600px); neither is needed just to avoid clipping. `showLineNumbers={false}` hides the gutter; `wrap` wraps long lines instead of scrolling horizontally.

Config editors: `<CodeBlockEditor bind:value bind:valid bind:validating bind:schemaUnavailable schema={jsonSchema} placeholder showDownload downloadBaseName disabled />` + a status badge row driven by the bindables (validating → 'Checking…' spinner; !valid → 'Invalid'; valid+schemaUnavailable → 'YAML parses'; valid → 'Valid YAML'). Grows to content (floor via `minHeight`, default 10rem) and scrolls rather than clips whenever its height is constrained; cap it yourself via `maxHeight` (any length) or `scroll` (=600px). Visually identical to CodeBlock. `language` (same union, default `"yaml"`) switches highlighting; live validation runs only for `"yaml"` — for other languages `schema` is ignored and `valid` stays true. The download button's extension/MIME follows the language (.yaml/.json/.py/.sh). Validation errors pair what happened with a fix (schema pointers render as `model.learning_rate`, types as plain words); when the schema fails with no field to point at, `schemaFallbackFix="..."` overrides the generic fix line with app-specific guidance.

components.name: collapsible
components.description: Expandable/collapsible section.
usage: `Collapsible.Root bind:open` + `Collapsible.Trigger chevron="start"` wrapping a Label sectionHeader → folding config/detail sections.

components.name: command
components.description: Searchable menu: a text field over a filtered, keyboard-navigable list of items, with groups, an empty state and a footer that stays in view. Reads as a DropdownMenu.
usage: `<Command.Root>` holds a `Command.Input`, a `Command.List` of `Command.Group`s (each a `Command.GroupHeading` and a `Command.GroupItems` of `Command.Item`s, with `Command.Separator`s between), a `Command.Empty`, and an optional `Command.Footer`. Put it in a `Popover.Content class="w-120 p-0"` for a searchable menu, or on the page as a standalone search list.

Filtering: by default Command filters and ranks the items itself against each item's `value` (plus any `keywords`). When the caller filters (its own match rule, a sort, a server search), pass `shouldFilter={false}` and render only the matching items; bind the input with `bind:value` to read the query.

`Command.Input` is an `InputGroup` with the search icon at its start. Controls that belong in the field, such as a sort toggle (`Tabs.List variant="segmented"` with icon-only triggers and an `aria-label` on each), go in as its children and sit at its end.

`Command.Item` takes `onSelect` (Enter or click) and `disabled`, which skips it in arrow-key navigation and dims it; say why in a `title`. The arrow keys move the highlight; pass `loop` on the root to wrap from the last item to the first. It takes DropdownMenu.Item's `variant` (`destructive`), `inset`, `typography` and `justify`, so a row is built the same way in both menus.

Mark the current pick with `data-checked={item.value === current}`: the item's trailing check shows on it, so the menu opens showing what's picked. Every item reserves the check's width, so rows line up whether or not one is checked.

`Command.Empty` shows when no item is left: "No file matches “report”." names the query. With the built-in filter that happens on its own. With `shouldFilter={false}` Command counts every mounted item, so while a query is typed leave out the static rows (an "All files" row, the footer) or Empty never shows.

`Command.Footer` sits below the list, outside its scroll, so it stays in view however long the list is ("Show all 240 files"). A `Command.Item` in the footer is still reached by the arrow keys; give it `forceMount` if it should stay while a built-in filter runs.

Headings, items and separators take DropdownMenu's own variants (`dropdownMenuGroupHeadingVariants`, `dropdownMenuItemVariants` through `commandItemVariants`, `dropdownMenuSeparatorVariants`), so the two menus can't drift apart. Style an item's row layout with `class`; don't restyle the highlight.

components.name: console-utils
components.description: className merge helper cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge with the rounded-interactive extension). Re-exported as $lib/utils in scaffolded apps.

components.name: copy-button
components.description: Copy-to-clipboard control that owns its own copied state.
usage: Icon beside a value: `CopyButton value={job.id} label="Copy job ID" title={job.id}` — `label` is the accessible name, so say what is being copied rather than "Copy", and pass the full value as `title` whenever the visible text is truncated.

Value inside the control: pass the value as children (`<CopyButton value={id} label="Copy blueprint ID">{id}</CopyButton>`) and the whole thing becomes one copy target with one hover, instead of a 16px icon beside plain text. The hit area follows automatically — children give the `inline` size, icon-only gives the 36px `icon` size.

Feedback: a check mark replaces the glyph for 1500ms (`feedbackDuration`) and a toast fires on both success and failure, so a mounted `<Toaster />` is a prerequisite. Pass `toast={false}` where the inline check is feedback enough — a table of IDs, where a toast per copy is noise — and the component announces the copy to screen readers itself instead. `successMessage` / `errorMessage` override the wording; `onCopy(copied)` hooks anything else.

Inside a row that navigates: `stopPropagation` keeps the click off the row's own handler (and off an enclosing anchor). Reveal-on-hover is the Button axis, `visibility="hover"`, which needs `group` on the row — but not when the value is inside the control, since it would fade the value too.

Copying without a button: `copyText(text)` is exported from the same subpath for a labelled action that happens to copy (a "Copy CSV" button in a dialog footer). It resolves to whether the write landed.

components.name: counter
components.description: Odometer for a numeric count: a pill by default, or bare so any number on the page can tick.
usage: Count: `Counter value={412}` rolls only the digit places that changed; past 999 it abbreviates (`1.2K`, `123K`, `1.2M`) so it never grows a fifth column, and the exact number stays in its title + accessible label.

Absent vs zero vs loading: omit the component entirely when there is no count, pass `value={0}` for an empty one, and `value={null}` while it is still loading (reserves the same width so nothing reflows when it arrives).

At least, for a list you cannot size: `Counter value={103} atLeast` renders `103+` when the caller has loaded 103 rows and knows only that more exist (keyset pagination, a capped query). The number is the caller's own, not a rounded threshold, and the accessible label reads "at least 103". Past 999 the abbreviation truncates instead of rounding, so `1250` shows `1.2K+` and never claims rows nobody loaded. `atLeast` is ignored on `value={0}`, where it would state nothing.

Three axes, each one thing: `variant` is the treatment (`pill`, the default, or `bare`), `tone` is colour (`solid` or `muted`, and `muted` still reads as muted on a bare counter), and `size` is the box (`sm` for dense rows like tables and list items). Inside a tab strip use `Tabs.Count`, which re-colors it for the active/inactive trigger.

A number anywhere, not just a pill: `variant="bare" size="inherit"` drops the pill and the mono face and takes the typography of whatever it sits in, so a headline figure, a table cell or a number in running text can roll. It sits on the surrounding baseline and reserves no width of its own, so it can be dropped mid-sentence: `Processed <Counter value={n} variant="bare" size="inherit" exact /> of 2,000 rows.` Size and weight come from the parent (`<span class="text-6xl">`), and the digit row tracks the line height, so it works at any scale.

Decimals: `decimals={2}` keeps two places (`0.97`, `1.00`) instead of rounding to a whole number, rounding half up like `Math.round(v * 100) / 100`, and is never abbreviated. Use it for a score or a rate; a count stays a whole number.

Exact digits: `exact` turns off the `1.2K` abbreviation and rolls the whole number. Use it where the reader is meant to read the figure rather than glance at it (a headline, a total in a sentence); leave it off in chrome, where a fifth column would reflow the layout.

components.name: dialog
components.description: Modal dialog for forms and confirmations.
usage: Open from a button: `<Dialog.Trigger>{#snippet child({ props })}<Button variant="outline" size="sm" {...props}>…</Button>{/snippet}</Dialog.Trigger>`.
Content = Dialog.Header (Title + Description) + Dialog.Body (form fields) + Dialog.Footer justify="between" pairing `outline` Cancel and `cta` Submit, both size="sm" typography="mono".

components.name: dropdown-menu
components.description: Contextual action menu.
usage: Trigger via child snippet spread onto a Button (profile menu: `variant="accent"` avatar + chevron, rounded-full).
Styled triggers: `DropdownMenu.Trigger variant="filter"` for toolbar/list filter dropdowns; `variant="input"` for form-field-styled dropdowns in pickers.
`DropdownMenu.Content align="end" class="min-w-64"`; items `justify="between"` with a trailing icon; `closeOnSelect={false}` for in-menu toggles (dark mode); Separator before Sign Out.

Section headings: `DropdownMenu.Label` for a standalone heading, `DropdownMenu.GroupHeading` inside a `Group`. Both render in the console's section-header treatment by default (10px mono, uppercase, muted, more space above than below so the heading binds to the rows it introduces), so a heading recedes rather than competing with its items. Set no type or colour classes on them; if a Label is carrying a row of content rather than a heading, override with `class`.

components.name: dropzone
components.description: File-upload drop target with per-phase snippets.
usage: `<DropZone.Root size="compact" multiple ariaLabel="Upload files">` in file pickers, {#snippet idle()} / dragging() / uploading()} states; `size="fill"` fills an entire empty panel.
idle = icon + DropZone.CaptionStack (Title + Action + Hint); uploading = `<Spinner size="lg" />` + Title.

components.name: empty-state
components.description: Placeholder for lists, tables, and panels with no content.
usage: `variant="list"` inside list/log containers ("No matching logs found.").
Point at the fix with inline links: `Button variant="link" size="inline"` inside the muted prose.

components.name: input
components.description: Single-line text input.
usage: `variant="search"` + placeholder + bind:value — search boxes in toolbars and log viewers (Search jobs…).
default variant for form fields; `variant="filter"` — search field inside filter/dropdown popovers; `variant="login"` pairs with input-group login.

components.name: input-group
components.description: Input with attached addons and buttons.
usage: Credential field: `InputGroup.Root variant="login"` + `InputGroup.Input variant="login" type="password"` + `InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end"` holding an `InputGroup.Button size="icon-sm"` eye toggle (aria-label for show/hide).

components.name: item
components.description: List-row unit for files, sessions, and uploads.
usage: File/attachment row: `variant="outline"` + Item.Media (file icon) + Item.Content (Item.Title + Item.Description with size · type).

Data row: `variant="rowItem"` + Item.Row of Item.Column column="grow|wide|mid|status" typography="mono" — truncated mono ids with a ghost icon copy button, a status Badge column, and Item.Actions holding icon buttons with visibility="hover" (the standard job/session/file row).
`variant="banner"` for banner-style rows; the phase axis (pending | uploading | complete | error) + Item.Status track upload lifecycles.

components.name: kbd
components.description: Keyboard-shortcut display.
usage: `Kbd.Group` holding one `Kbd.Root` per key (⌘ K, Ctrl Shift P).

components.name: label
components.description: Text label for form fields, sections, and headings.
usage: `variant="sectionHeader"` — the ubiquitous mono uppercase heading above values and form sections, in card content and collapsible triggers.
`variant="tableColumnHeader"` — dashboard table/list column headers; `variant="selectionSubHeader"` — sub-header over selection rows in pickers.
`variant="fieldError"` — validation error under a field; `variant="workbenchHeader"` — workbench panel headers; `variant="pagination"` — 'Page X of Y'.
default variant + for= on form inputs.

components.name: labs-utils
components.description: Labs domain helpers plus cn() re-exported from console.

components.name: loading-bar
components.description: Indeterminate loading bar for route/navigation transitions.
usage: Mount once in the root layout and gate on navigation: `{#if navigating.to}<LoadingBar />{/if}` (SvelteKit `navigating` from `$app/state`). Presentational only — it does not read navigation state itself.
`position="bottom"` pins it to the viewport bottom; always fixed + full-width. For navigation only. Work inside a page uses `Progress`: a value when the total is known, `value={null}` when it is not.

components.name: logo
components.description: Archetype AI brand logo mark.
usage: Headers: `<Logo class="h-6 w-auto" />` next to the app title; sizes sm | default | lg.

Compact lockup: `variant="compact"` is the stacked social/avatar artwork (~1.6:1 instead of the wordmark's ~5.4:1). Use it where a horizontal wordmark will not fit — square tiles, avatars, narrow sidebars, splash marks. Defaults to `variant="default"`.

Sizing is shared: both variants honour size sm | default | lg (h-4 | h-6 | h-8) and take their width from the artwork aspect, so compact renders far narrower at the same height. Prefer default or lg for compact.

components.name: menubar
components.description: Branded app header with logo, partner-logo slot, action children, and built-in dark-mode toggle.
usage: Top of every dashboard shell; children render as right-side actions — `Button variant="link" class="text-muted-foreground no-underline hover:underline"`.

components.name: popover
components.description: A floating panel anchored to a trigger, on DropdownMenu's surface and motion. Padded by default; hosts a Command for a searchable menu.
usage: DropdownMenu vs Popover + Command: a plain list of actions or choices is a `DropdownMenu`. Reach for `Popover` + `Command` only when the list needs a search field, which DropdownMenu can't host (its typeahead takes the keystrokes), or a footer that stays in view while the list scrolls.

`<Popover.Root bind:open>` with a `Popover.Trigger` and a `Popover.Content`. The trigger is unstyled: pass a `Button` through its `child` snippet (`{#snippet child({ props })}<Button variant="outline" {...props}>…</Button>{/snippet}`) so it looks like every other trigger.

`Popover.Content` is portalled, offset 4px, `w-72` and padded (`p-4`, children `gap-4`) for free-form content. For a searchable menu, put a `Command` inside and pass `class="w-120 p-0"` (any width, no padding) so the Command sits flush. `align="start"` lines it up with a trigger at the start of a row.

A searchable menu's trigger is a combobox: give the `Button` `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded={open}` and an `aria-label` naming what it picks (a combobox isn't named by its text, unlike a button), and bind its `ref`. On a pick, close and hand focus back to the trigger: `open = false; tick().then(() => triggerRef?.focus())`. `Popover.Close` wraps a control that should close it directly.

components.name: progress
components.description: Progress bar: fills to a known value, or sweeps while the total is unknown.
usage: A rolling percentage above the bar is composed, not a prop: wrap a bare Counter and the bar in a `flex flex-col gap-2.5`, with the figure as `` and a `text-muted-foreground text-lg` unit beside it. Mark the whole figure row `aria-hidden`: the bar already announces the value through `aria-valuenow`, so the number drawn beside it is presentation, not a second thing to read out.
Pair with a large mono readout: `{value}%` beside the bar.
`size="sm"` for compact/inline progress (upload rows); always aria-label.

Unknown total vs not started: `value={null}` is work whose total isn't known (a running eval that reports rows scored but no row count). The bar sweeps, drops `aria-valuenow`, sets `aria-busy` and marks `data-indeterminate`. Pass `value={0}` for work with a known total that hasn't moved yet. Show what is known beside the bar (`1,276 rows scored`), never a made-up percentage.
Reduced motion holds the sweep still in the centre of the track, so it can't be read as partly done.
`variant="running"` paints the bar in `atai-neutral`, the colour the console uses for a running job (see Badge's status recipe). `success` and `critical` are for finished work.

components.name: scatter-chart
components.description: Scatter-plot card for embeddings and cluster views; composes BackgroundCard + Chart.
usage: `<ScatterChart title icon data categoryKey="cluster" categories={{ q1: 'Cluster A', … }} xMin xMax yMin yMax xTicks yTicks />` — data rows are { x, y, <categoryKey> }; categories map drives legend + series colors.
Streaming: append rows and set `maxPoints` for a sliding window.

components.name: score-bento
components.description: Score hero: a 0..1 score as a field of one hundred cells painted in the tone, revealed from the bottom-right corner while the figure rolls up to its value.
usage: `ScoreBento value={0.97} label="Macro F1"` paints the whole field and rolls the figure to `0.97` (a bare `Counter` with `decimals={2}`). The value is 0..1 and shown to two decimals; round the same way (`Math.round(v * 100) / 100`) anywhere else the page prints this score, so the hero and a list can't disagree on a digit.

Unscored vs in flight vs scored: `value={null}` renders the empty field and an em dash (no score yet, or a failed run). While the run is going, pass `status="running"` with `value={null}`: a single diagonal sweeps the empty field back and forth without claiming a score, and `valueText` + `meta` carry what is known (`valueText="1,276" meta="rows scored"`). `status="completed"` with a value reveals the field from the corner on first paint and lands the `eyebrow` once the last cell does.

`status` takes the agent service's eval and optimization statuses as they come (`pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`); only `running` and `completed` move, the rest are still. Reduced motion stills both.

`tone` picks the colour: `neutral` (the default) paints from the theme's foreground and works for any score; `babyblue` and `yellow` are brand fills; `warning` is the system's warning colour, for a score that needs attention; `slate` is graded, so the score picks its step (below). Which tone a score wears is the caller's decision, e.g. a band map kept beside the thresholds. A score paints every cell in the tone's token at full strength in both themes, so the colour and the figure carry it, not an amount of cells; with no score the cells show the bento's background. A new colour is a new tone in `scoreBentoFieldVariants` and `scoreBentoInkVariants`, not a call-site override.

`tone="slate"` is the one graded tone: the score's tenth picks a step on the slate scale, 50 at 0.05 up to 900 at 0.95, run the other way in dark (950 up to 100) so a high score still stands furthest from the page, with the ink flipping to white from 500. Use it where the score itself should colour the bento; the fixed tones paint the same colour at every score.

Around the figure: `eyebrow` is a short line above it (a verdict such as "Great"), `meta` a line under it, `valueText` replaces the two-decimal figure with a caller-formatted string, and `trailing` is a top-right line such as a delta against the previous run. `help` is a plain-words explanation of the label, behind an info disc in the top-right corner. `help` renders a Tooltip, so the page needs a `Tooltip.Provider` above it; put one in the app layout rather than wrapping each bento.

`size="compact"` fits a side panel or another narrow column (a shorter field, `text-7xl` figure); `default` is the page hero. The bento sets no width or grid placement of its own: lay it out with `class` (`md:col-span-7 md:row-span-2` beside two `StatBento`s at `md:col-span-2`).

components.name: select
components.description: Single-choice dropdown (bits-ui).
usage: `Select.Root type="single" bind:value` + `Select.Trigger variant="input"` in forms; render a $derived label with a 'Select a …' fallback as trigger text.
`Select.Content > Select.Group > Select.Item value label` per option; default trigger variant in toolbars/headers.

components.name: sensor-chart
components.description: Time-series line-chart card with multi-signal support and sliding-window streaming; composes BackgroundCard + Chart.
usage: `<SensorChart title="ACCELERATION SENSOR" icon={AudioWaveformIcon} data={rows} signals={{ accel_x: 'Accel X', … }} yMin yMax yTicks />` — data rows are { timestamp: Date, <signalKey>: number }.
Streaming: append rows and set `maxPoints` (sliding window); `axis="y"` hides the time axis while streaming.

components.name: separator
components.description: Hairline divider.
usage: Horizontal between stacked sections; `orientation="vertical"` in multi-column layouts.

components.name: side-panel
components.description: Non-modal side panel for peeking at or inspecting one object without leaving the list it came from.
usage: Bind the panel to an object id, never to a row: `<SidePanel.Root open={selectedId !== null} onOpenChange={(o) => !o && (selectedId = null)}>`. Keep the id in the URL so the state survives refresh, back and sharing; the primitive itself never reads or writes the URL. Do NOT derive the panel's content straight from that id: the panel stays mounted while it closes, so the content would blank out before it leaves. Latch the last opened object instead, `let shown = $state(null); $effect(() => { const next = find(selectedId); if (next) shown = next; })`, and render from `shown`.

Peek vs inspect: content with no page of its own just fills `SidePanel.Body`. Content that has a full page renders the page's body component inside Body and puts the handoff ONCE, in the Header `actions` snippet, as an outline icon button beside the built-in Close: `<SidePanel.Header>{#snippet actions()}<Button variant="outline" size="icon" class="size-8" aria-label="Open full page" href={fullPageUrl}><ArrowUpRightIcon /></Button>{/snippet}<SidePanel.Title>…</SidePanel.Title></SidePanel.Header>`. Header actions are outline icon buttons at the sm height (`class="size-8"`, Button has no small icon size) so they read as one set with Close, pinned to the header's top-right, and match `size="sm"` Footer buttons; never repeat the handoff in the Footer.

It never renders an overlay or scrim and never traps focus or scroll: the list behind stays fully interactive, clicking outside does nothing, Escape closes. If the task needs the page blocked, use Dialog instead.
One panel at a time. Drilling in replaces Body's content and adds an in-panel back; it never opens a second SidePanel.
Read-mostly: actions inside are fine, but destructive confirmations spawn a Dialog over the panel. The panel does not own confirmation.

`size="sm"` (384px) for a record and its fields; `size="md"` (576px) when Body carries a preview, a chart or a code block; `size="lg"` (768px, capped at the window's width) when Body holds a full-size page section such as a scorecard or a confusion grid. `side="left"` only when the list itself lives on the right.

Header layout follows Dialog: a `space-y-2` block, so `SidePanel.Title` and then either `SidePanel.Description` (plain text) or `SidePanel.Meta` (badges, a status line, key/value metadata) stack full width. The `actions` cluster and the close sit absolutely at the top right, so the header reserves right padding and a long Title truncates rather than running under them. Give header actions the same bare icon treatment as the close via `sidePanelCloseButtonVariants`; keep `Description` when the subtitle is text, because it is what wires `aria-describedby` and `Meta` cannot.

Content renders in place (no portal) so Tab reaches it after the list; do not mount it inside a transformed ancestor, where `fixed` misplaces. Focus does not move on open. Header renders an outline icon Close by default (`showCloseButton={false}` to place `SidePanel.Close` yourself). `SidePanel.Footer` is optional: it holds the actions on the data being viewed, never Close or the full-page handoff. One primary action sits right; with `justify="between"` secondary actions (copy an id, compare) go first and land left.

size:
so it still fits a window narrower than the panel
      lg

components.name: slider
components.description: Range slider (bits-ui).
usage: `<Slider type="single" bind:value max={100} step={1} aria-label="…" />`; also the scrub control inside video-player.

components.name: sonner
components.description: Toast notifications (svelte-sonner themed for the DS).
usage: Mount `<Toaster />` once at the app root; fire `toast.success('3 files uploaded')` / `toast.error(...)` from anywhere, `{ description }` for a second line.

components.name: spinner
components.description: Loading indicator.
usage: `size="lg"` in upload/empty panels; default size with `class="size-4"` for inline row/status loaders; `variant="braille"` for terminal-style loaders; Button embeds it via its `loading` prop.

components.name: stat-bento
components.description: Small figure bento: a label top-left, the value bottom-right, one line of context bottom-left. ScoreBento's quiet sibling.
usage: `StatBento label="Accuracy" value="0.94" meta="1,203 of 1,276"`. `value` is a string the caller formats (`0.94`, `12%`, `3m 20s`), so the bento never guesses at precision or units.

Missing vs pending: pass `value="—"` when the figure does not exist, and say why in `meta` while it is still coming (`meta="when complete"`). Omit `meta` when there is nothing to add; the value keeps its bottom-right place either way.
Where the bento is too narrow for `meta` and the value side by side, the value wraps under the context line instead of widening the bento, so the bento can go in a two- or three-up grid of any width.

It sits on the card surface, not a tone, so a coloured `ScoreBento` beside it stays the only coloured thing. It sets no height or grid placement: size and lay it out with `class` (`min-h-28` in a side panel, `md:col-span-2` beside a bento).
`help` renders a Tooltip info disc in the top-right corner, so the page needs a `Tooltip.Provider` above it; put one in the app layout.

components.name: switch
components.description: On/off toggle switch (bits-ui).
usage: `bind:checked` + aria-label; sizes sm | default | lg.

components.name: table
components.description: Data table.
usage: Log/event tables: width-classed Table.Head columns, `Table.Body class="font-sans text-xs"`, level cells colored with status tokens (text-atai-critical for error rows).
Mono body (`typography="mono"` on Table.Body) for id-heavy tables; pair with `EmptyState variant="list"` when empty.
Header rows never take the data-row hover — `Table.Header` neutralizes it; don't cancel `hover:bg-*` from consumer code.

Sortable columns: `Table.Head sortable direction={col === sort ? order : null} onSort={() => setSort(col)}`. The primitive owns the affordance, the three-state indicator and `aria-sort`; the consumer owns the sort state, so a Sort menu and the headers can drive the same state and stay in step. Mark only the columns the API can actually order by. Non-sortable heads are unchanged and simply are not clickable.

components.name: tabs
components.description: View and section switcher.
usage: The look is set once, on `Tabs.List`; triggers take it from the list and have no styling props of their own beyond `variant="icon"`.
Page-section tabs (Progress | Logs | Artifacts): `Tabs.List` (`variant="line"` is the default) with plain text triggers and a `Tabs.Content` per tab; always `Tabs.Root bind:value`.
A second strip nested inside a section's panel: `Tabs.List size="sm"`, so it reads as a level below the page's strip. `size` exists on `line` only.
Mode or view switch over the same content (Library | File IDs | Upload, Share | Count): `Tabs.List variant="segmented"` with text triggers and no `Tabs.Content`.
Icon view toggle (list/grid) or sort direction: `Tabs.List variant="segmented"` + `Tabs.Trigger variant="icon"` with an icon, and a `title` or `aria-label` on each trigger.

Count on a trigger: `<Tabs.Trigger value="logs">Logs <Tabs.Count value={logCount} /></Tabs.Trigger>` — an odometer pill that abbreviates past 999 (`1.2K`) so the strip never reflows. Pass `value={null}` while the count is still loading (it reserves the width), `value={0}` for an empty tab, and omit `Tabs.Count` entirely for a tab that has no count at all.

Count on a tab that cannot be sized: `<Tabs.Count value={loaded} atLeast />` renders `103+` for a keyset-paginated tab that knows only how many rows it has so far. Prefer it over dropping the count entirely, which reads as "none".

components.name: textarea
components.description: Multi-line text input.
usage: Feedback/description fields under a Label sectionHeader; bind:value + placeholder.

components.name: theme
components.description: darkMode singleton controller syncing the `dark` class on <html>.
usage: `darkMode.set(window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches)` on startup; `darkMode.toggle()` from a menu item or icon button; `darkMode.current` for reactive reads.

components.name: toggle
components.description: Pressed-state button (bits-ui).
usage: Icon-only by default (aria-label required); `variant="outline"` for icon + text.

components.name: tooltip
components.description: Hover hint.
usage: Wrap the app/section in `Tooltip.Provider delayDuration={200}`.
Field help: `Tooltip.Trigger variant="info"` is a filled 16px disc holding a mono `i` — pass it no children, it renders its own glyph. Explanation goes in `Tooltip.Content`.

`aria-label` on the info trigger is required and is the caller's: name what is being explained (`aria-label="About Detection Log"`). The glyph is `aria-hidden`, so without a label the button has no accessible name.

The info disc squares against `Counter size="sm"`'s height on purpose — a section title, its `Counter` and its info disc in one `flex items-center gap-2` row is the intended cluster, the solid pill reading as the count and the muted one as the meaning. 16px is also exactly the height of a `Label variant="sectionHeader"` box, so the disc sits level with the title rather than towering over it.
`size="lg"` is the 20px disc, for a cluster built around `Counter size="default"` (`h-5`) rather than a section label. `size` is inert on the other trigger treatments, which have no box.
`variant="inlineLink"` — underlined trigger flowing inside prose (supported file requirements).

The arrow centres itself on the trigger on all four sides and protrudes half its box — `arrowClasses` is for its ink or size, not for centring corrections. If a tip looks off, it is a bug in `tooltipArrowVariants`, not something to counter-shift at the call site.

components.name: video-player
components.description: Media-playback card whose seek track doubles as a timeline: named marker windows, tinted highlight bands and bindable playback state. Composes Card + AspectRatio + Button + Slider.
usage: `<VideoPlayer src muted />` for the standard controlled player; `controls={false}` for ambient/looping footage. `preload="metadata"` by default, so `duration` is known before the first play.

Playback state: `bind:time` / `bind:duration` / `bind:paused` mirror the media element out, and `time` and `paused` are writable - assigning to `time` seeks, assigning `paused = false` plays. That is how another view drives the player.

Markers: `markers={[{ start, end, label?, color? }]}` in **seconds, not fractions** draws one focusable dot per window on the seek track. Clicking a dot expands it into a range pill, seeks to its start and plays; one is expanded at a time, and `bind:activeMarker` is its index (or null). Scrubbing by hand, or a click on the video surface, collapses it. `loopActiveMarker` loops playback inside the expanded window.

Linked brushing: `highlights={[{ start, end, color? }]}` tints regions another view is pointing at (brushing in), and `onMarkerHover(index | null)` fires on hover **and focus** so a hovered marker can highlight the matching row elsewhere (brushing out).

Two lifecycle traps when `src` changes: a new `src` remounts the player and Svelte's media bindings write your bound values into the fresh element, so reset `time = 0` and `paused = true` yourself or a stale position becomes the new clip's start; and `bind:duration` holds the previous clip's value until `loadedmetadata`, so reseed `duration` from a known length if marker geometry must be right on the first frame (`duration === 0` collapses every marker to the left edge).

`controlsVisibility="always"` pins the control bar open - required whenever markers must stay clickable during playback, since the default `"auto"` fades the bar (and the markers with it) 2.5s into playback. `formatTime` replaces the mm:ss clock in the time readout and the marker captions.

Style hooks: `data-slot` on `video-player`, `-video`, `-overlay`, `-controls`, `-time`, `-markers`, `-marker` (carries `data-expanded`), `-marker-caption`, `-highlight`. A per-marker `color` inks the outline and fill via `currentColor`.
Marker seeking needs an origin that serves HTTP Range requests; against one that does not, seeks silently do nothing (serve the clip from a blob URL instead).
